verdicts.title: An exact closed walks series formula for the complexity of regular graphs and some related bounds
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The complexity of a graph is the number of its labeled spanning trees. In this work complexity is studied in settings that admit regular graphs. An exact formula is established linking complexity of the complement of a regular graph to numbers of closed walks in the graph by way of an infinite alternating series. Some consequences of this result yield infinite classes of lower and upper bounds on the complexity of such graphs. Applications of these mathematical results to biological problems on
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns graph complexity defined as the number of labeled spanning trees and its relation to closed walks in regular graphs, with no mention of Euler characteristic, Tseitin formulas, or resolution proof width.

verdicts.title: Computing Euler characteristics using quantum field theory
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: This paper explains how to use quantum field theory techniques to find formal power series that encode the virtual Euler characteristics of $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ and related graph complexes. Finding such power series was a necessary step in the asymptotic analysis of $χ(\mathrm{Out}(F_n))$ carried out in the authors' previous paper.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns Euler characteristics of Out(F_n) and graph complexes via quantum field theory techniques, which shares the 'Euler characteristic' vocabulary but does not address Tseitin formulas, resolution proof width, or any connection to proof complexity.
